The circles $r=4\sqrt{2}$ and $r=8\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta $ intersect at points $A$ and $B,$ as shown above. What are the polar coordinates $(r,\theta )$ of the point $A?$ Express the polar angle $\theta \in [{0}^{∘},\text{ }\,{360}^{∘})$ in degrees.

$(r,\theta )=(${{field-1}}$,$
{{field-2}}${}^{∘})$
question.worked_solution:
To determine the polar coordinates of the intersection points, we will solve the following system of equations for $r$ and $\theta :$

$$
\{\begin{aligned}r=8\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  \\ r=4\sqrt{2}\end{aligned}
$$

We begin by setting the equations equal to each other and solving for $\theta .$ This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}8\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  & =4\sqrt{2} \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  & =\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Solving this equation in the interval $[{0}^{∘},\text{ }\,{360}^{∘}),$ we obtain ${\theta }_{1}={45}^{∘}$ and ${\theta }_{2}={135}^{∘}.$ 

Also, notice that $r=4\sqrt{2}$ at both intersection points.

Therefore, polar coordinates of the point $A$ are 

$\,$ $(r,\theta )=(4\sqrt{2},{135}^{∘}).$
